A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same causal-velocity research, with matching authors, central methods and theoretical results. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite substantial experimental revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original synthetic and benchmark causal-discovery results, plus experiments comparing velocities recovered using true and estimated scores.

after.justification: V2 reports original synthetic and benchmark results, expanded method comparisons, and quantitative sample-size and score-estimation experiments.

M1.justification: The two-stage score-to-velocity estimator, velocity families and fitting objective remain. A limited inference change is reported: causal-direction scoring uses the absolute-value variant in v1 Section 8 and the squared-value variant in v2 Section 7. MLP, ANM and LSNM are otherwise renamed V-NN, V-ANM and V-LSNM.

E1.justification: Synthetic coverage is substantially revised: the non-injective Periodic SCM disappears, Velocity and Sigmoid generators change, and non-Gaussian ANM/LSNM benchmarks are added. V2 also evaluates continuous-only Tübingen pairs. The five Tagasovska benchmarks remain in Appendix E.2; SIM-C was already described as evaluated in v1.

E2.justification: The external comparator set expands from LOCI to include CDS, IGCI, RECI and CGCI in synthetic and retained-benchmark comparisons. V2 also reports LOCI's HSIC and likelihood variants separately instead of the single best-LOCI summary used in v1 (Tables 2–3 and Appendix E.2).

E3.justification: Synthetic experiments change from n=2,000 to n=5,000, with added n=1,000 subsampling and n=100–10,000 sensitivity protocols. V2 switches evaluation from absolute to squared discrepancies, replaces the kernel/HYBRID grid with Stein-Gaussian and KDE-Laplace configurations, and revises the stated basis-model learning rate in Appendix D.2.

E4.justification: V2 substantially expands the qualitative score-estimation probes into quantitative sample-size, score-error and directional goodness-of-fit analyses (Figures 4–5 and 7; Tables 8–9). It adds subsampling and continuous-only Tübingen checks. V1's individual altitude–temperature case study and several direct velocity-comparison illustrations are removed.

E5.justification: V2 newly reports medians and first/third quartiles for score errors and goodness-of-fit over 100 datasets (Figure 5; Tables 8–9). V1 lacks comparable dispersion summaries. This documents variability across generated datasets, without establishing additional training seeds or repeated runs.

E6.justification: Synthetic and benchmark result sets are extensively replaced or expanded. For example, B-QUAD's SIM-G accuracy is 96% in v1 Table 3 and 94% with KDE in v2 Table 3, with AUDRC 99 in both; changed settings prevent interpreting this as a same-setting decline. V2 additionally tabulates SIM-C, continuous-Tübingen, new comparator and sample-size results.

T1.justification: The correspondence, consistency and identifiability results and Appendix A–C proofs remain substantively unchanged after renumbering. Appendix D.1 adds explicit Gaussian-score and marginalization derivations. However, new equations (68) and (71) omit the negative inverse-variance factor required by the Gaussian score identity retained in Appendix A.3.

C1.justification: The abstract is unchanged, and the introduction retains the same principal contributions: causal-velocity parametrization, noise-agnostic score-based discovery, identifiability analysis and consistency. Calling the estimator likelihood-free makes an existing property explicit rather than introducing a new core claim.

C2.justification: V2 adds distributional interpretations of causal curves in Section 3.1 and explanations concerning Gaussian versus non-Gaussian noise, continuous-only Tübingen performance and outlier sensitivity in Sections 7.2–7.3 and Figure 5. These refine the retained central limitation that successful discovery depends on accurate score estimation.

D1.justification: V2 adds detailed synthetic-generation parameters, score regularization and bandwidth choices, hardware/timings, benchmark trimming/resampling instructions and Tübingen exclusions. These are largely new disclosures, not proof of changes to previously unspecified settings. Conversely, v1's explicit curvature-penalty formula and coefficient disappear, and v2's two-layer main-text network description conflicts with its three-layer Appendix D.2 description.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations supporting the expanded baselines, Causal Discovery Toolbox, Adam and bandwidth selection, and acknowledges Tu et al. (2022) on velocity-based causal discovery. The Kidger reference is removed. RESIT framing becomes clearer, while the principal positioning relative to ANMs, LSNMs, cocycles and normalizing flows remains.

P1.justification: V2 substantially rewrites the functional-discovery background, velocity interpretation, method explanation and experimental narrative. The standalone consistency section moves into Section 5 before identifiability; experiments acquire separate Results and Sample Size subsections, and experimental appendices are reorganized. The abstract and most proof text remain stable.

P2.justification: Figures 1–3 are redrawn or recomposed, and new goodness-of-fit and sample-size plots replace several qualitative illustrations. Main and appendix tables are substantially restructured around expanded comparators and estimator-specific results, with new parameter and quartile tables. These changes go well beyond numerical updates or renumbering.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's LOCI-only external comparisons and mainly qualitative score probes, v2 offers broader empirical scrutiny and quantitative sensitivity reporting, alongside better implementation disclosure. These gains are moderated by lost penalty details and new inconsistencies in Gaussian-score formulas and network depth, which weaken reproducibility and confidence in the added diagnostics. The net improvement is therefore limited.
